correctness.rationale: Subtracting phase updates gives the exact coordinates u+=u+h sin(u)(cos(u)-cos(v)), v+=v-3h cos(u)sin(v) at P=(pi,pi). For 0<h<2/3, |1-3h|<1 gives stable v contraction and positive near-unity u multiplier; geometric |v_n/u_n| decay and center negativity force u_n→0 off u=0, while u=0 contracts exponentially. Independent Taylor expansion at v=0 gives (u+/u)=1-hu²/2+hu⁴/8+O(u^6); hence for Y=u^-2 the drift is h+h(3h-1)/(4Y)+O(Y^-2+rho^n). Summing the absolutely summable corrected increments proves Y_n=hn+(3h-1)log n/4+C+o(1). For h<1/3 the weighted graph Laplacian norm <=3 yields a strict gradient descent map with invertible derivative, global torus diffeomorphism, exactly four critical phase classes and vanishing-area stable manifolds of the source/two saddles. The remaining nonhyperbolic equilibrium is locally attractive; hence almost every orbit reaches it. Invariant u=0 circle is the complete exponential basin away from the source. Independent rational Taylor and finite oscillator iterations (h=0.13,.2,1/3,.48,.6) reproduced the coefficient and convergence of the renormalization; the proof, not those tests, establishes globality.

value.rationale: Three repulsive oscillators on an isosceles triangle form the smallest geometrically frustrated phase network, with natural critical edge-weight 1/2. Linearization has a unit multiplier and cannot resolve convergence. The exact slow typical relaxation, step-sensitive subleading log cancellation at h=1/3, and exceptional geometric stable curve together give a complete motivated boundary classification in the stated small-step regime.

limitations: Fixed repulsive triangle weights and identical oscillators only; local h in (0,2/3), global h in (0,1/3).
